meaning.en: To endure, or be willing to endure, extremely serious hardship, danger, pain, pressure or sacrifice because a person, cause or goal matters greatly.
meaning.zh: 為了某人、某項理念或一個十分重要的目標而承受，或願意承受，極大的困難、危險、痛苦、壓力或犧牲。

benefits.en: He went through fire to protect his family.
benefits.zh: 這個表達可以把多年痛苦、危險和犧牲濃縮成較簡潔有力的句子。

benefits.en: The expression communicates more than willingness to help. It suggests very deep commitment.
benefits.zh: 這個表達不只是表示願意幫忙，而是顯示十分深厚的承諾和忠誠。

benefits.en: The second sentence presents the experience as far more painful and serious.
benefits.zh: 第二句把這段經歷形容得更加痛苦和嚴峻。

benefits.titleEn: It Can Praise Determination and Sacrifice
benefits.en: This highlights both the difficulty and the person’s determination.
benefits.zh: 這個表達同時突出困難的程度和當事人的決心。

benefits.en: The expression can criticise situations in which somebody is expected to sacrifice too much. Important Benefit Warning 重要提示 An idiom is not automatically better than a plain expression. Use go through fire only when the hardship is genuinely extreme and the dramatic tone serves a clear purpose.
benefits.zh: 這個表達也可以批評某人被要求作出過多犧牲的情況。 慣用語不一定比直接說法更好。 只有在困難確實十分嚴峻，而且強烈語氣具有明確作用時，才應使用 go through fire。

origin.statusEn: Exact Short-Form Origin Unknown; Related Longer Form Documented
origin.statusZh: 確切簡短形式來源不明；相關較長形式已有記錄

history.en: Psalm 66:12 in English Bible translations contains the image of people who “went through fire and water” before reaching safety. This demonstrates an old religious and literary image of surviving severe trials, but it does not prove when the exact modern expression was invented. Major learner dictionaries document the longer form go through fire and water rather than establishing a first use of go through fire alone. Cambridge describes the longer expression as UK old-fashioned.
history.zh: 英文《聖經》詩篇第66篇第12節包含人們經過「火與水」後到達安穩之地的畫面。 這顯示以火與水象徵嚴峻考驗的意象由來已久，但不能證明確切的現代表達是在何時創造。 主要學習字典收錄的是較完整的 go through fire and water，而未能確認 go through fire 這個簡短形式的首次使用時間。

history.en: The physical image of surviving fire came to represent enduring pain, danger and sacrifice. The shorter go through fire retains the strongest part of that image and is understood as a dramatic metaphor.
history.zh: 捱過真正火焰的畫面逐漸用來代表承受痛苦、危險和犧牲。 簡短形式 go through fire 保留了這個意象中最強烈的部分，成為富有戲劇性的比喻。

origin.memoryEn: Surviving fire requires exceptional strength; going through fire for a goal means refusing to give up despite exceptional hardship.
origin.memoryZh: 捱過火焰需要非凡力量；為目標 go through fire，便表示即使面對極大艱辛也不放棄。
